slides.texte_overlay:
What to do when you feel
behind in life
Stop comparing your chapter one to someone's chapter twenty. Social media shows highlights, not the years of struggle behind them. Your timeline is yours.
Write down what you've already done. Skills learned, problems solved, people helped. Feeling behind often means forgetting how far you've actually come.
Choose one area to focus on. Health, money, career or relationships. Trying to fix everything at once is how people stay stuck for years.
Start small, but start today. A ten-minute workout, a first savings transfer, one job application. Action is the only real cure for feeling behind.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Small daily progress is the fastest way to stop feeling stuck.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Small daily progress is the fastest way to stop feeling stuck.

slides.texte_overlay: Spend time with people who encourage you. Some friends make you feel late, others make you feel ready. Choose carefully who you listen to.
Remember that many people found their path later. Writers, founders and athletes started in their 30s, 40s and beyond. It's not too late for you either.
